problem: Leadership argued that speed and quality were being sacrificed when people work from home.
title: Yahoo ends remote work for employees starting in June 2013
context: A memo from Yahoo's HR head was leaked in February 2013.
decision_made: Require remote employees to work from a Yahoo office by June.
action_taken: The memo reached full-time remote workers and, per some reports, those working from home a day or two a week.
observed_outcome: Reaction was largely critical, including from long-time telecommuters, though some defended it. Yahoo and its leaders declined to comment on the controversy. No productivity results were found.
lessons: A bold policy communicated through a leaked memo can overshadow its substance.
limitations: Only reaction was documented. Fortune said the rule was in practice less drastic than the memo implied.

claims.claim_text: Yahoo told employees with remote arrangements to work from an office starting in June 2013.
Fortune called it a bold move with bad delivery and noted the rule was less drastic in practice than the memo implied.
